sections.title: Vestirse and Ponerse
sections.content:
Spanish has specific reflexive verbs for clothes:
- **Vestirse** (e → i): general action of getting dressed (*me visto, te vistes, se viste, nos vestimos, se visten*).
- **Ponerse**: putting on a specific article of clothing (*me pongo los zapatos*). The *yo* form has an irregular stem: **me pongo**.
- **Quitarse**: taking off clothing (*me quito la chaqueta*).

items.spanish: Me visto rápidamente por la mañana.
items.english: I get dressed quickly in the morning.

items.spanish: Hoy me pongo una camisa blanca.
items.english: Today I am putting on a white shirt.

items.spanish: ¿Por qué no te quitas el abrigo?
items.english: Why don't you take off your coat?

items.spanish: Carlos se peina antes de salir.
items.english: Carlos combs his hair before leaving.

sections.content: In Spanish, use definite articles with body parts and clothing, not possessives: say *Me pongo la chaqueta* (not *mi chaqueta*) and *Me lavo las manos* (not *mis manos*).
